item.title: The union that could skyrocket Winter, Smotrich and Feiglin
item.description: איחוד אפשרי בימין עשוי לשנות משמעותית את מפת המנדטים: לפי סקר כאן חדשות, רשימה משותפת של וינטר, סמוטריץ' ופייגלין זוכה ל-11 מנדטים. ללא וינטר, החיבור בין הציונות הדתית לזהות עומד על 6 מנדטים.

item.title: Yisrael Beytenu unveils election slate as key figures exit
item.description: Lieberman’s party reveals its candidates for the 26th Knesset, while some prominent figures resign and others are left off the slate.

item.title: Royal visit: South African Queen and Princes get inside look at MDA
item.description: South African Queen, Princes and Princesses tour MDA’s advanced facilities in Israel, with one royal calling the experience ‘life-changing.’

item.title: Not standard issue: IDF soldier’s ‘serial killer’ patch lands him in trouble
item.description: Armed IDF soldier filmed at Tel Aviv train station wearing ‘Serial Killer’ and other unusual patches; IDF says he will face disciplinary proceedings.

item.title: Fake abduction report triggers major police, IDF response
item.description: A late-night call claiming three Israelis were being abducted sent police and IDF forces rushing to Hizma-only for investigators to allege the group had entered the village voluntarily and falsely reported an abduction.

item.title: IDF planning on operating in Lebanon in coming hours, explosions expected in northern Israel
item.description:
The Kiryat Shmona Municipality announced that IDF forces are expected to operate in Lebanon within the next hour, and that explosions may be heard in Kiryat Shmona and communities across the Galilee.
At this stage, normal routines remain in place and no special instructions have been issued to the public.

item.title: Jerusalem mugger pulls knife at ATM, victim pulls gun
item.description: Knife-wielding suspect allegedly attacks civilian withdrawing cash at Jerusalem ATM; intended victim draws his pistol and shoots, severely wounding him.

item.title: Zamir to Israel’s enemies: Attack us, pay a ‘very heavy price’
item.description: IDF Chief Eyal Zamir oversees surprise ‘Breaking Dawn 2.0’ exercise testing readiness for multi-front war and warns enemies of an immediate, heavy price.

item.description: Lebanese report: Two killed in Israeli strike in Nabatieh area in the south

item.title: Supreme Court: ‘Extremely bleak’ picture of violence in Samaria
item.description: Supreme Court orders state to coordinate return of three Palestinian Arabs to their Samaria homes within 14 days, sharply criticizing enforcement failures.

item.title: Givat Shaul shooting: Suspect shot in attempted robbery
item.description:
Following an initial investigation by officers from the Moriah Police Station, who arrived at the scene of the shooting incident in the Givat Shaul neighborhood in Jerusalem, police suspect that the incident was an attempted robbery during which the suspect was shot by one of those involved.
The suspect was evacuated to the hospital in serious condition, according to medical officials. Police said the incident was criminal in nature. Officers are operating at the scene, and the circumstances are under investigation.

item.title: Givat Shaul shooting: Man in his 30s in serious condition
item.description:
A man in his 30s was seriously wounded in an incident on Kanfei Nesharim Street in Jerusalem, suffering a penetrating injury.
Magen David Adom paramedics treated him at the scene and evacuated him to Shaare Zedek Medical Center.

item.title: Initial reports of a suspected shooting incident in Jerusalem's Givat Shaul neighborhood
item.description: The police are looking into a report of a suspected shooting incident in the Givat Shaul neighborhood in Jerusalem. Police forces are en route to the scene, and the incident is under review.

item.title: 84-year-old killed in tragic balcony fall while building sukkah
item.description: An 84-year-old man was killed in Efrat after falling from his balcony while preparing to build a sukkah at his home.

item.title: ‘Don’t mess with us’: Netanyahu warns Iran of crushing response
item.description: Netanyahu warns Iran against attacking Israel, says its regime is weak and faltering, and vows to complete a mission that will reshape the Middle East.

item.title: U.S. lawmakers arrive in Samaria with bold recognition push
item.description: A delegation of U.S. senators and representatives visited Samaria as lawmakers pledge new state legislation to recognize Judea and Samaria and drop the term West Bank.

item.title: Police arrest suspect in thefts on Route 446
item.description:
Police officers from the Judea and Samaria District arrested a man in his 20s from Qibya on suspicion of involvement in a series of robberies and vehicle thefts on Route 446.
According to the suspicion, in one incident he stole a vehicle during a meeting arranged for the exchange of parts, and in another he staged a collision and rammed a vehicle in order to force it to stop and then rob it. The suspect was taken into custody at the conclusion of his interrogation.

item.title: Tzvika Foghel quits Otzma Yehudit ahead of upcoming election
item.description: Ben-Gvir praised Tzvika Foghel as a “true fighter" after the MK announced he will not run with Otzma Yehudit in the upcoming election.

item.title: Bennett publishes Together party list
item.description:
Naftali Bennett, chairman of the “Together" party, published his party slate for the Knesset ahead of the elections.
Former Finance and Transportation Ministry director-general Keren Turner will be placed second on the list, former Communications Ministry director-general Liran Avisar Ben-Horin will be third, and former Ra’anana Municipality director-general Michal Hirsch NagrI will be fourth. Knesset member Eitan Ginzburg will be fifth.
They will be followed, in order, by: Yonatan Shalev, Bruria Naim Arman, Amir Strugo, Nisan Zeevi, Orly Harel, Shahar Varon, Esti Ayalon Kovo, Jeremy Saltan, Zvi Plotnitsky, Olesya Kantor, Mati Gil, Tomer Weiner, Tami Muziel, Yael Stern and Amit Barda.

item.title: No Elections Needed: Moses' last day
item.description: On his final day, Moses does not look back - he prepares Israel for the future, passes the mantle to Joshua, and leaves behind a timeless lesson in leadership, humility and faith.

item.title: Water Authority: Water supplies to residents and agricultural sector continuing as normal
item.description: The Water Authority and the Ministry of Energy reported that the systems remain stable and that water supplies to residents and the agricultural sector are continuing as normal. At the same time, it was decided to purchase a dedicated stock of membranes for desalination facilities, and the public was asked to use water efficiently and responsibly.

item.title: Zamir warns IDF must be ready for surprise attack across all fronts
item.description: IDF Chief Eyal Zamir says Israel’s military must remain ready for a surprise attack as commanders test responses to a rapidly escalating multi-front war.

item.title: Survey: 94% surge in number of doctors who left Israel within 3 years
item.description: A Tel Aviv University study found that approximately 1,370 doctors left Israel for at least one year between 2023 and 2025, nearly twice the number a decade earlier.

item.title: Possessing a rocket: Hamas terror cell thwarted in northern Jordan Valley
item.description: The IDF announced that in a joint operation with the Israel Police and Shin Bet in the Akraba area, a Hamas terrorist cell was thwarted, 10 terrorists were apprehended and a rocket was located.

item.title: Adidas faces boycott calls over Israeli veteran featured in campaign
item.description: Sportswear giant Adidas is facing boycott calls over a campaign in Israel featuring former IDF soldier Shalev Biton, who lost his left leg after being wounded while fighting near Gaza.

item.title: Profile 70 | IDF moves to increase number of combat soldiers
item.description: The Medical Corps and Manpower Directorate have developed a new medical fitness classification intended to immediately expand the pool of candidates eligible for combat service.

item.title: 250 days alone at sea: Israeli sailor makes history in grueling round-the-world race
item.description: Daniel Pinsky, a 35-year-old sailor from Ariel, is the first Israeli to take part in the Golden Globe race; over 250 days, he will sail alone around the world, with no stops, crew, or GPS, relying only on paper maps and compasses.

item.title: Called for Jihad | Terrorist turned Instagram into channel for terror incitement
item.description: A serious indictment has been filed against a terrorist who disseminated inciting content on social media, praised terrorist attacks, and called for attacks against Jews.
